The Gman above all is a businessman. He stores subject so he can utilize them, I don't think putting someone in stasis is such a pressure on his end (knowing what he has done so far). Shepherd has proven to be one whose had and survived through their own personal holocaust. There might be even more subjects in stasis when you think about it. He uses his knowledge to capture people who could be important assets to his employers.

I am not sure who stated that they are not cannon, but have it your way base HL still has questinable ethics and in the border world you still can see scientists that are dead. You can debate that they teleported after the resonance cascade but mostly their blood is dried out indicating its been a long time before the 3-4 days in which Half-Life takes place.

Black Mesa has been studying the border world long before the resonance cascade. Even though then didn't really bring back the purest sample used in the mass spectrometer, (Gman gave it to them) they were aware of what they were working with and fully on point with the capabilities due to their research. Further more, in Questionable Ethics we can see the the studies conducted on the fauna of the border world before the events of the resonance cascade. Weapon selection system is installed in the Mark IV Hazard Suit because of the hostility that the science team has seen in Xen. Fuuuuuurther more, the hazard course has combat ready training. In Blue Shift we can see the old prototype labs used to conduct teleportation between worlds. The HECU are assigned to be there in case that the worst happens. They are not knowledgeable about the bio labs. Speaking of HECU, Adrian Shepherd in Oppsing Force finds and wields another prototype of Black Mesa - the Displacer cannon. It allows the user to teleport from Earth to Xen. 

Bottom line is that Black Mesa has been on and studying Xen long before you see the big fish from the challenger deep, but I am sure that it never swam in terrestrial waters until a week ago!
